detail: Girls' school struck by US Tomahawk cruise missile adjacent to IRGC naval compound. label: Oil/Gas Facilities Hit
note: DAY 146 (July 15-23): US strikes on Kharg Island tanker operations — the Curacao-flagged M/T Belma disabled off Kharg July 15 and re-struck July 17 — plus the collapse of Chabahar's maritime surveillance tower add to the tally (50+). Kharg handles ~94% of Iran's crude exports (Kpler). PRIOR — DAY 137 (July 7-14): KUWAITI OFFSHORE OIL RIG STRUCK — Iran hit an offshore oil drilling platform in Kuwaiti territorial waters Jul 12 (1 worker injured) plus 3 northern border posts (Kuwait Defense Ministry, Col. Saud Abdulaziz Al-Atwan) — the first strike on Kuwaiti offshore energy infrastructure of the war, helping drive Brent's +9.59% Jul 13 spike. Iran also struck 5 tankers (Jul 7 & 13-14) incl. the Qatari LNG carrier Al Rekayyat (engine room afire). PRIOR — DAY 103 (June 10): ASSALUYEH PETROCHEMICAL COMPLEX HIT — an explosion was reported at the Assaluyeh petrochemical complex (~50% of Iran's petrochemical output) during the June 10 CENTCOM ~49-Tomahawk strike wave across Iran; no further strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure occurred June 11-15 as the US-Iran deal was finalized (signing set for June 19). DAY 101 (June 8): Israel struck a PETROCHEMICAL COMPLEX near MAHSHAHR (Khuzestan) producing ballistic-missile precursor materials, part of a large IAF strike that also hit air-defense sites at Tehran, Isfahan and Tabriz; Iran additionally claimed (UNVERIFIED) that the June 9 US strikes near Hormuz hit reservoirs serving ~20,000 people. IEA: 44+ energy assets severely damaged across 9 countries + Kharg Island 50+ targets Apr 7 + Asaluyeh (South Pars, ~50% of petrochemical production) — worst since combined 1973 + 1979 oil shocks. DAY 73 (May 11): SECOND KHARG OIL SLICK CONFIRMED — Windward AI to Fox News Digital reports a second slick (~12-20 km²) detected May 10 11:00 local; PRIMARY slick remains 52-71 km² per Windward + Orbital EOS SAR; drifting south toward Qatar/UAE EEZ; UN warns of potential 'environmental catastrophe.' Total estimated release ~80,000 bbl. Mixed signals vs Day 71 'much reduced' Copernicus read (Greenpeace) — persistent SAR signature contradicts optical dispersion read; second slick May 10 indicates ongoing release. Iran (Iranian Oil Terminals Company + MFA) denies leak as 'psychological warfare.' DAY 70 (May 8): Suspected ~45 km² oil slick detected near Kharg Island via Copernicus Sentinel-1/2/3 imagery May 6–8 — potentially largest spill since war start; origin unconfirmed; Pentagon declined to confirm tracking; Greenpeace projects spill could reach UAE/Qatar/Saudi shores within 7–10 days. Earlier oil-release events observed near Qeshm and Lavan (Mar–Apr 2026) linked to reported strikes on infrastructure.
source: IEA / DoD / Bloomberg / QatarEnergy / Reuters / satellite imagery
detail: IEA (Mar 23): At least 44 energy assets severely damaged across 9 countries — 'very severe, worse than the combined 1973 and 1979 oil shocks.' IEA released record 400M barrels from strategic stockpiles (US: 172M from SPR). Iraq declared force majeure on all foreign-operated oilfields (production collapsed from 4.2M to ~1.2-1.4M bpd). Combined Gulf production cuts exceed 10M bpd (JPMorgan). Iran: Kharg destroyed, South Pars Phases 3/4/5/6 struck. Qatar: Ras Laffan 12.8 MTPA lost (17% of LNG exports, 3-5yr repair). SAMREF (Saudi) struck. Kuwait: Mina al-Ahmadi hit. Haifa BAZAN refinery. Bahrain Bapco under force majeure. Iran sanctions lifted on ~140M barrels at sea (30 days). Jones Act waived 60 days.

label: Nuclear Facilities Struck
note: DAY 137 (July 7-14): BUSHEHR NUCLEAR POWER PLANT NOT DAMAGED — despite US strikes in and around Bushehr Jul 8 and Jul 14, an Iranian official confirmed NO damage to the nuclear power plant (Nour News); count unchanged. PRIOR — DAY 113 STATUS (per signed MOU): Iran's nuclear sites (Natanz/Esfahan/Fordow) are assessed largely destroyed with little significant activity since the war (ISIS/CSIS satellite imagery); the most recent confidential IAEA figure in the public record put Iran's 60% HEU at 440.9 kg (a 7.9% rise over the prior report) — unverified since Iran barred IAEA access to bombed facilities — and the 14-point MOU signed June 17 commits Iran to down-blend the stockpile on Iranian soil under IAEA supervision (IAEA benchmark: ~42 kg of 60% HEU, if further enriched to 90%, is theoretically enough for one weapon). Fordow, Isfahan UCF, Natanz (3x), Bushehr (4x), Arak Heavy Water, Ardakan yellowcake (struck again Apr 7 — Shahid Rezayee Nejad facility), Yazd, Khondab (severely damaged, no longer operational) — IAEA zero access — Grossi: 'cannot rule out radiological release necessitating evacuation of areas as large as major cities'
detail: Fordow enrichment facility struck Day 1 with B-2/GBU-57 MOPs — assessed inoperable. Isfahan UCF struck Day 1. Natanz struck 4 times — underground FEP 'severely damaged.' Day 29: US-Israeli airstrikes hit Ardakan yellowcake and Khondab Heavy Water Complex. Bushehr struck 4 times — most recently Apr 4 when 1 physical protection staff killed, nearest strike impacted 75m from site perimeter. IAEA DG Grossi: strikes could cause 'severe radiological accident with consequences beyond Iran's borders.' Rosatom evacuated 198 Russian staff from Bushehr Apr 4. Iran possesses 440.9 kg of 60%-enriched uranium — enough for approximately 10 nuclear weapons if further enriched. IAEA has zero access to enrichment facilities. Grossi: 'I do not believe that Iran's nuclear program can be eliminated solely by military action.' Source: IAEA / Rosatom / Pentagon / Bulletin of Atomic Scientists.

label: Airports Damaged
note: DAY 146 (July 15-23): Continued US strikes on Iran's southern airfields during the 12-night July cycle (Iranshahr airport re-hit within the composite south-central target set) raise the count to 11+. PRIOR — DAY 137 (July 7-14): IRANSHAHR AIRPORT HEAVILY BOMBED Jul 8 — flight-operations building and meteorological station damaged, 1 firefighter killed (IRNA/Mehr). PRIOR — DAY 100 (June 7, Sunday): KUWAIT INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT REMAINS CLOSED / at reduced capacity after the June 3 Iranian drone/missile strike on Terminal 1; rolling Gulf flight suspensions continue (Wego/Gulf Business). DAY 96 (June 3, Wednesday): KUWAIT INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT — a terminal was severely damaged by an Iranian drone/missile strike and the airport briefly closed; Kuwait Airways and Jazeera Airways resumed operations later the same day from a different terminal. Iran + region — 3 Tehran airports struck Apr 7 (Bahram, Mehrabad, Azmayesh); DAY 57 (Apr 25): Tehran IKIA RESUMES international flights after 56-day hiatus — first departures to Istanbul, Muscat, Medina; Iran Air domestic Tehran-Mashhad inaugural; Mehrabad continues domestic + select diplomatic ops
source: ACLED / Flightradar24 / Iranian state media / Al Jazeera / FlightRadar24
detail: Mehrabad (Tehran), Shiraz TAB 6, Tabriz TAB 2 runways cratered in first wave. Dubai International Airport struck by drone Mar 16. April 7: strikes on three Tehran airports (Bahram, Mehrabad, Azmayesh) targeting Iranian air force aircraft and helicopters. Regional airspace closures affect 52,000+ commercial flights. DAY 57 (Apr 25): Tehran Imam Khomeini International Airport (IKIA) resumed international flights after a 56-day shutdown — Iran state TV confirmed departures to Istanbul, Muscat (Oman), and Medina (Saudi Arabia); FlightRadar24 showed at least four Istanbul-bound departures Saturday morning. Iran Air operated its inaugural post-war domestic flight Tehran-Mashhad. Routes to Baku, Najaf, Baghdad, and Doha scheduled in coming days. Iran Airports & Air Navigation CEO Mohammad Amirani indicated eastern Iran (Mashhad, Zahedan, Kerman, Yazd, Birjand) will be prioritised for transit. Mehrabad continues domestic + limited diplomatic ops.

label: Bridges Destroyed
note: DAY 146 (July 15-23): US strikes July 17 severed multiple Hormozgan crossings — the Bandar Abbas-Rudan highway/rail bridge (closed to traffic), a railway junction, a road tunnel and the Bandar Khamir bridge — with AP assessing the aim was to cut Iran's main port from routes to Tehran (≥7-8 killed, ~20 injured; IRNA). Count now ≥18+. PRIOR: Israel launched wide-scale bridge/railway strikes Apr 7 — Qom bridge, Kashan railway bridge (2 killed, 3 injured), Tabriz-Zanjan freeway, Karaj railway — IDF issued 12-hour Farsi warning to avoid trains — Karaj B1 bridge double-tap Apr 2 (8 killed, 95 wounded) — Qasmieh Bridge (last south of Litani) destroyed Apr 8, partially reopened, struck again Apr 16 cutting humanitarian access — all Litani River bridges destroyed in Lebanon (150,000 cut off)
source: Satellite imagery / IDF / Lebanese media / Iranian state media
detail: April 7: IDF launched 'wide-scale wave of strikes targeting dozens of infrastructure sites' — confirmed hits on key bridge near Qom, railway bridge in Kashan (2 killed, 3 injured), Tabriz-Zanjan freeway, railway infrastructure in Karaj. IDF issued 'urgent warning' in Farsi to stay away from trains/railways for 12 hours. Appears to be opening phase of Trump's 'Bridge Day.' Previous bridges destroyed in Kermanshah, Lorestan, Khuzestan provinces. Karaj B1 bridge Apr 2 double-tap killed 8, wounded 95. Lebanon: All Litani River bridges destroyed — 150,000 people cut off in southern Lebanon. Qasmieh Bridge (last bridge south of Litani) destroyed Apr 8, partially reopened, struck again Apr 16 cutting humanitarian access. IDF permanent buffer zone south of Litani.

label: Water/Desalination Facilities Struck
note: DAY 146 (July 15-23): The Bonji desalination plant intake station at Jask (Hormozgan) was destroyed in a US strike July 17, cutting drinking water to ~10,000 people across 20 villages (Iran national water company / ISNA). The US did not confirm targeting the plant and said damage may be spillover; Iran's Energy Ministry acknowledged 'attacks on power infrastructure' for the first time the same day. This is an emerging humanitarian-law flashpoint (Atlantic Council warning). Earlier in the war US strikes damaged water reservoirs near Sirik (June, ~20,000 residents affected), and Iranian retaliation set two Kuwaiti power+desalination plants ablaze July 17-18 (Kuwait relies on desalination for ~90% of its drinking water).
source: Iran national water company / ISNA / CENTCOM / Atlantic Council / Al Jazeera
detail: Bonji (Jask) desalination plant intake station destroyed July 17; ~10,000 people across 20 villages lost drinking water. Kuwait, which relies on desalination for ~90% of its drinking water, saw two power+desalination plants set ablaze by Iranian strikes July 17-18.
